answer: Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the lotus checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. The signal graph is rebuilt each epoch, as a result the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the garden audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 3 times its size, so a group of 18 keys loses far more than 18 single identities would. That is 30 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
